ORDINANCE XLV OF 1997
ORDINANCE XLV OF 1997
PAKISTAN ELECTRIC POWER REGULATORY
AUTHORITY ORDINANCE, 1997
An Ordinance to provide for the
establishment of the National Electric Power Regulatory Authority
[Gazette of Pakistan, Extraordinary,
Part I, 7th March, 1997]
No.F.2(1)/97‑Pub., dated 7‑3‑1997.‑‑The
following Ordinance made by the President on the 2nd March, 1997 is hereby
published for general information:‑
Whereas it is expedient to provide
for the National Electric Power Regulatory Authority to improve the efficiency
and availability of electric power services, including by mobilizing
generation, transmission and distribution of electric power through private
ownership and for matters connected therewith and incidental thereto;
And whereas the National Assembly is
not in session and the President is satisfied that circumstances exist which
render it necessary to take immediate action; '
Now, therefore, in exercise of the
powers conferred by clause (1) of Article 89 of the Constitution of the Islamic
Republic of Pakistan, the President is pleased to make and promulgate the
following Ordinance:‑‑
CHAPTER I
GENERAL
1. Short title, extent and
commencement.‑‑(1)
This Ordinance may be called the Pakistan Electric Power Regulatory Authority
Ordinance, 1997.
(2) It extends to the whole of
Pakistan.
(3) Sections 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9,
12, 13, 14, 48 and 49 shall come into force at once and the remaining
provisions shall come into force on such date as the Federal Government may, by
Notification in the Official Gazette, appoint, and different dates may be so
appointed for different provisions.

And whereas the National Assembly is

Now, therefore, in exercise of the

CHAPTER II
ESTABLISHMENT OF AUTHORITY
3. Establishment of the Authority.‑‑(1) As soon as may be,
after the commencement of this Ordinance, the Federal Government shall establish
a National Electric Power Regulatory Authority consisting of a Chairman to be
appointed by the Federal Government and four members one from each Province to
be appointed by the Federal Government in consultation with the respective
Provincial Governments:
Provided that no person shall be
appointed as a Chairman or member who has attained the age of seventy years. '
(2) There shall be a Vice‑Chairman
of the Authority, appointed from amongst the members for a period of one year,
by rotation, in the following order, namely:‑
(i) the member representing Province
of Balochistan;
(ii) the member representing
Province of North‑West Frontier;
(iii) the member representing
Province of the Punjab; and
(iv) the member representing
Province of Sindh.
(3) The Chairman shall be an eminent
person of known integrity and competence with at least twenty years of relevant
experience in Government, law, or electric utility business.
(4) Every member shall be a person
of known integrity and competence with at least fifteen years of related
experience in Government, law, business, engineering, finance, accounting,
economics or a related discipline:
(5) The Chairman and members shall,
unless resigned or removed earlier as hereinafter provided, hold office for a
term of four years and shall be eligible for re‑appointment for a similar
term.
(6) In the case of death,
resignation or removal of a Chairman or a member, another Chairman or, as the
case may be, a member may be appointed in his place for the unexpired term of
such Chairman or member.
(7) No act or proceeding of the
Authority shall be invalid by reason only of existence of a vacancy in, or
defect in, the constitution of the Authority.
(8) The principal office of the
Authority shall be in Islamabad and it may set up offices at such place or
places as it may deem appropriate.

CHAPTER II
ESTABLISHMENT OF AUTHORITY
6. Powers and functions of the
Authority.‑‑(1)
The Authority shall be responsible for regulating the grant of licences for
generation, transmission and distribution of electric power.
(2) In particular and without
prejudice to the generality of the foregoing power, the Authority shall‑‑
(a) grant licences for generation,
transmission and distribution of electric power;
(b) approve tariff, rates, charges
and other terms and conditions for supply of electric power services by the
generation, transmission and distribution companies;
(c) prescribe procedures and
standards for investment programmes by generation, transmission and distribution
companies;
(d) review organizational affairs of
the transmission an(' distribution companies to avoid any adverse effect on the
operation of the electric power and for continuance and efficient supply of
such power;
(e) develop and enforce performance
standards for generation, transmission and distribution companies;
(f) encourage uniform industry
standards and code of cone‑ict for generation, transmission and
distribution companies;
(g) establish a uniform system of
accounts by generation, transmission and distribution companies;
(h) tender advice to the public
sector projects;
(i) submit reports to the Federal
Government in respect of activities of the generation, transmission and
distribution companies;
(j) levy fees, with the approval of
the Federal Government, for grant of licences and renewal thereof;
(k) 'prescribe fines , for
contravention of the provisions of this Ordinance; and
(l) perform any other function which
is incidental or consequential to any of the aforesaid functions.
(3) In performing its functions
under this Ordinance, the Authority shall, as far as prazticable, protect the
interests of consumers and companies providing electric power services in
accordance with the guidelines laid down by the Federal Government.

7. Remuneration, etc., of Chairman
and members.‑‑(1)
The Chairman and members shall be paid such emoluments as may be determined by
the Federal Government but such emoluments shall not be less than the salary
and perquisites admissible to the Judge of the High Court and shall not be
varied to their disadvantage during their term of office:
Provided that the Chairman and
members shall not, during their term of office, engage themselves in any other
service, business, vocation or employment:
Provided further that for two years
after the conclusion of their terms of office, the Chairman and, as the case
may be, a member shall not enter into the employment of, or accept any advisory
or consultancy relationship with any person engaged in the generation,
transmission or distribution of electric power in Pakistan or any related
undertaking.
(2) During their term of office, the
spouses and children of the Chairman and members shall not have any direct or
indirect financial interest, or have connection with any company connected with
the generation, transmission or distribution of electric power nor such spouses
and children shall, enter into employment of, or accept any advisory or
consultancy relationship with such companies.

following Ordinance:‑‑
CHAPTER III
LICENCES
32. Tariffs.‑‑(1) The Authority
shall, within one year from the commencement of this Ordinance, determine
procedures and standards for approval, modification or revision of rates,
charges and terms and conditions for transmission, inter‑connection
services, distribution services and power sales to consumers by the licensees.
(2) The Authority while determining
the standards referred to in subsection (1) shall‑‑
(a) protect consumers against
monopolistic prices;
(b) permit licensees to recover
their costs of providing electric power service so as to attract financing for
capital improvements and new construction and to meet the requirements of
companies approved investment and power acquisition progra gores approved by
the Authority;
(c) encourage efficiency in
licensee's operations and quality of service;
(d) encourage economic efficiency in
the electric power industry;
(e) permit distribution companies to
recover all costs incurred by those companies under power purchase contract;
(f) keep in view the adjustment of
the subsidies made by the Federal Government and manner and extent of its
recovery; and
(g) determine tariffs so as to
minimize the economic distortions.
(3) The procedures established
under. subsection (1) by the Authority shall include‑‑
(a) time frames for tariff
applications and decisions by the Authority;
(b) opportunity for customers and
other interested parties to participate meaningfully in the tariff approval
process; and
(c) refund protection for customers
while tariff decisions are pending.
(4) The rates and charges for sale
of electric power to bulk‑power consumers shall be regulated by the
Authority subject to the prior approval of the Federal Government.

WAPDA, the advice of the Authority shall be sought by the agency planning to

granting approval to any project, consider‑‑

published for general information:‑
Whereas it is expedient to provide
for the National Electric Power Regulatory Authority to improve the efficiency
and availability of electric power services, including by mobilizing
generation, transmission and distribution of electric power through private
ownership and for matters connected therewith and incidental thereto;
And whereas the National Assembly is
not in session and the President is satisfied that circumstances exist which
render it necessary to take immediate action; '
Now, therefore, in exercise of the
powers conferred by clause (1) of Article 89 of the Constitution of the Islamic
Republic of Pakistan, the President is pleased to make and promulgate the
following Ordinance:‑‑
CHAPTER IV
ADMINISTRATION
48. Rules.‑‑(1) The Authority may,
with the prior approval of the Federal Government, make rules to carry out the
purposes of this Ordinance.
(2) Without prejudice to the
generality of the foregoing powers, such rules may provide for‑‑
(a) procedure for seeking
nominations of members from the Provincial Governments;
(b) the form and manner of
application to be made for a licence for generation, transmission or
distribution facilities;
(c) the fees and documents to be
accompanied with the applications for licences;
(d) determination of rates, charges
and other terms and conditions of licences;
(e) procedure for recovery of fines
as arrears of land revenue;
(f) publication of rates and charges
of electricity consumption, procedure for metering, billing and collection of
electric power charges by the licensees;
(g) procedure for resolving disputes
amongst the licensees and consumers and the licensees;
(h) procedure for submission of
various reports to the Federal Government and the manner of preparation of such
reports;
(i) procedure for inquiry and
investigation into the affairs of an applicant for a licence and for any
contravention of any provision of this Ordinance;
(j) the manner and procedure of show‑cause
notices;
(k) safe, effective and
environmental free supply of electric power;
(l) performance and industrial
standards for supply of electric power; and
(m) standards for Investment Programmes
for transmission companies and Investment and Power Acquisition Programmes for
distribution companies. ,
